translations.idiomatic: Compilation officials received meal-conversion money: the Supervisor of the National History, forty thousand cash; History Office compilers, Direct History Office, and provincial chiefs and deputies, thirty-seven strings five hundred; reviewers and compilers, thirty-five strings — all per longstanding precedent.)

sentences.zh: 有特旨添支。

translations.literal: Some received supplemental allowance by special edict.
translations.idiomatic: Others received supplemental allowance by special edict.

sentences.zh: 如紹興元年指揮：館職，寺監丞、簿、評事，台法、主簿，寺正、司直，博士，添職錢一十貫。

translations.literal: As in the Shaoxing 1 directive: archives posts, temple and directorate vice directors, registrars, and reviewers, censorate legal examiners and chief clerks, temple directors and case reviewers, erudites — added ten strings in office salary.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shaoxing 1 directive, holders of archives posts, temple and directorate vice directors, registrars, and reviewers, censorate legal examiners and chief clerks, temple directors and case reviewers, and erudites received an added ten strings in office salary.

sentences.zh: 六年指揮：五寺、三監、秘書、大宗正丞，太常博士，著作、秘書、校書郎，著作佐郎，正字，大理寺正、司直、評事，台簿，刪定官，檢、鼓、奏告院，特支米三石計議、編修官二石。

translations.literal: Under the 6 directive: vice directors of the Five Courts, Three Directorates, Secretariat, and Court of the Imperial Clan; Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite; Compilers, Secretariat Proofreaders, Assistant Compilers, Standardizers, Judicial Review Director, Inspector, and Reviewing Official; Censorate Chief Clerk; Text Reviser; Inspection, Drum, and Memorial Announcement courts — special disbursement of three piculs of rice; Planning and Compilation Officials, two piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Under the year-6 directive, vice directors of the Five Courts, Three Directorates, Secretariat, and Court of the Imperial Clan; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Erudite; compilers, Secretariat proofreaders, assistant compilers, standardizers, and Judicial Review director, inspector, and reviewing official; the censorate chief clerk; text revisers; and staff of the Inspection, Drum, and Memorial Announcement courts received three piculs of rice as a special disbursement; Planning and Compilation Officials received two piculs.

sentences.zh: 祿粟及隨身、兼人：宰相，一百石，紹興：三公，侍中，中書、尚書令，左、右僕射同平章事，並為宰相。

translations.literal: Grain salary and personal attendants and attendants: Chancellor, one hundred piculs; Shaoxing: Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, Secretarial and Palace Directors, Left and Right Grand Councilors with Concurrent Councilor in the Department of State Affairs — all counted as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Grain salary, personal attendants, and attendants: the chancellor received one hundred piculs; under Shaoxing the Three Excellencies, Palace Attendant, Secretarial and Palace Directors, and Left and Right Grand Councilors with Concurrent Councilor in the Department of State Affairs all counted as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 隨身七十人。

translations.literal: Seventy personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 知樞密院事，參知政事，樞密副使，同知樞密院事，一百石，隨身五十人。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Vice Grand Councilor, Vice Commissioner, Associate Commissioner — one hundred piculs; fifty personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Vice Grand Councilor, Vice Commissioner, and Associate Commissioner each received one hundred piculs and fifty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 太師、太傅，太保，少師，少傅，少保，一百石，舊制百五十石。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Grand Tutor, Grand Protector; Junior Preceptor, Junior Tutor, Junior Protector — one hundred piculs; old regulations one hundred fifty piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand and Junior Preceptors, Tutors, and Protectors received one hundred piculs each; under the old regulations they had received one hundred fifty piculs.

sentences.zh: 隨身一百人。

translations.literal: One hundred personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 太尉，一百石，隨身五十人。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal, one hundred piculs; fifty personal attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal received one hundred piculs and fifty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 節度使，祿粟已具奉祿類。

translations.literal: Military commissioner — grain salary already listed under salary categories.
translations.idiomatic: For military commissioners, grain salary is already set out under salary categories.

sentences.zh: 元隨五十人，承宣使，元隨五十人。

translations.literal: Fifty original followers; commissioner for court announcement, fifty original followers.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty original followers; the commissioner for court announcement likewise had fifty original followers.

sentences.zh: 觀察使，防禦使，元隨三十人。

translations.literal: Observation commissioner and defense commissioner, thirty original followers each.
translations.idiomatic: Observation and defense commissioners each had thirty original followers.

sentences.zh: 團練使，已上並具奉祿類。

translations.literal: Training commissioner — all above already listed under salary categories.
translations.idiomatic: For the training commissioner and all ranks above, stipends are already listed under salary categories.

sentences.zh: 元隨三十人。

translations.literal: Thirty original followers.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty original followers.

sentences.zh: 諸州刺史，同上。

translations.literal: Prefects of the various prefectures — the same as above.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects of the various prefectures — the same as above.

sentences.zh: 元隨二十人，通侍大夫，正侍大夫，宣正大夫，履正、協忠、中侍、中亮大夫，祿粟、傔人並具奉祿類。

translations.literal: Twenty original followers; Grand Master for Court Service, Grand Master for Direct Attendance, Grand Master for Proclaiming Rectitude, Grand Masters for Upholding Rectitude, Coordinating Loyalty, Central Attendance, and Central Brightness — grain salary and attendants already listed under salary categories.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty original followers; for the Grand Master for Court Service, Grand Master for Direct Attendance, Grand Master for Proclaiming Rectitude, and the Grand Masters for Upholding Rectitude, Coordinating Loyalty, Central Attendance, and Central Brightness, grain salary and attendants are already listed under salary categories.

sentences.zh: 捧日、天武左右廂都旨揮使遙郡團練使，五十石，傔十人。

translations.literal: Sun-Upholding and Heavenly Martial left and right wing commanders-in-chief with distant-prefecture training commissioner title — fifty piculs; ten attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders-in-chief of the Sun-Upholding and Heavenly Martial left and right wings holding distant-prefecture training commissioner titles received fifty piculs and ten attendants.

sentences.zh: （龍、神衛右廂都指揮使帶遙郡團練使同。）〉

translations.literal: (Dragon Guard and Divine Guard right wing commanders-in-chief with distant-prefecture training commissioner — the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (The same applied to Dragon Guard and Divine Guard right wing commanders-in-chief holding distant-prefecture training commissioner titles.)

sentences.zh: 殿前諸班直都虞候，諸軍都指揮使遙郡刺史，二十五石，傔五人。

translations.literal: Chief aide of the Hall Direct Guards of the Palace Forecourt and army commanders-in-chief with distant-prefecture prefect — twenty-five piculs; five attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The chief aide of the Hall Direct Guards of the Palace Forecourt and army commanders-in-chief with distant-prefecture prefect titles received twenty-five piculs and five attendants.

sentences.zh: （龍、神衛諸軍都指揮使帶遙郡刺史同。）〉

translations.literal: (Dragon Guard and Divine Guard army commanders-in-chief with distant-prefecture prefect — the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (The same applied to Dragon Guard and Divine Guard army commanders-in-chief holding distant-prefecture prefect titles.)

sentences.zh: 諸學士添支米已附於前，今載：觀文殿大學士，傔二十人。

translations.literal: Academicians supplemental rice has been given above; recorded here: Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture — twenty attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians supplemental rice appears above; recorded here: the Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture had twenty attendants.

sentences.zh: 觀文殿學士，資政、保和殿大學士，傔十人。

translations.literal: Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture; Grand Academicians of the Halls for Assisting Governance and Preserving Harmony — ten attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and Grand Academicians of the Halls for Assisting Governance and Preserving Harmony had ten attendants each.

sentences.zh: 資政、保和殿學士，龍圖、天章、寶文、顯謨、徽猷、敷文閣學士，傔七人。

translations.literal: Academicians of the Halls for Assisting Governance and Preserving Harmony; academicians of the Dragon Diagram, Heavenly Writ, Treasured Writ, Displaying Counsel, Manifest Worth, and Fixing the Text halls — seven attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Academicians of the Halls for Assisting Governance and Preserving Harmony and of the Dragon Diagram, Heavenly Writ, Treasured Writ, Displaying Counsel, Manifest Worth, and Fixing the Text halls had seven attendants each.

sentences.zh: 樞密都承旨，傔十人；

translations.literal: Chief Reception Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, ten attendants;
translations.idiomatic: The Bureau of Military Affairs Chief Reception Secretary had ten attendants;

sentences.zh: 副都承旨、諸房副承旨，七人。

translations.literal: Deputy Chief Reception Secretary and deputy reception secretaries of the various bureaus, seven.
translations.idiomatic: the Deputy Chief Reception Secretary and the various bureaus deputy reception secretaries had seven.

sentences.zh: 其餘京畿守令、幕職曹官，自十石、七石、五石至於二石各有等。

translations.literal: The rest — capital-area prefects and magistrates and secretariat and precinct staff — from ten, seven, and five piculs down to two piculs, each with its grade.
translations.idiomatic: All other capital-area prefects and magistrates and secretariat and precinct staff received graded allotments from ten, seven, and five piculs down to two piculs.

sentences.zh: 中書堂後官提點五房公事，逐房副承旨，自七人、五人至於一人各有數。

translations.literal: Behind the Hall of the Central Secretariat, officials who intendant the general affairs of the five bureaus and the deputy receivers of edicts for each bureau each had fixed numbers, from seven and five persons down to one.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the Central Secretariat hall, the officials who superintended the five bureaus and each bureau's deputy edict receivers were allotted fixed numbers of attendants, ranging from seven or five down to one.

sentences.zh: 因仍前製，舊史已書。

translations.literal: Following the former system, the old histories already record it.
translations.idiomatic: These arrangements followed earlier practice and are already recorded in the older histories.

sentences.zh: 凡任宰相、執政有隨身，太尉至刺史有元隨，餘止傔人。

translations.literal: In general, those who served as chancellor or chief administrator had personal attendants; from Grand Commandant down to regional inspector they had primary attendants; the rest had only retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In general, chancellors and chief administrators received personal attendants; from the Grand Commandant down to regional inspectors they received primary attendants; all other officials received only retainers.

sentences.zh: 紹興折色：凡祿粟每石細色六斗米麥中支。

translations.literal: Shaoxing commutation rates: for all salary grain, per picul six dou of fine-grade rice and wheat were disbursed in commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Shaoxing commutation rules, for every picul of salary grain six dou of fine rice and wheat were paid in commuted form.

sentences.zh: 管軍給米六分，麥四公。

translations.literal: For those administering troops, rice was six parts and wheat four parts.
translations.idiomatic: For troop administrators the allotment was six-tenths rice and four-tenths wheat.

sentences.zh: 隨身、元隨、傔人糧，每鬥折錢三十文，衣綢絹每匹一貫。

translations.literal: Grain for personal attendants, primary attendants, and retainers was commuted at thirty cash per dou; for clothing, silk and satin were one string per bolt.
translations.idiomatic: Rations for personal attendants, primary attendants, and retainers were commuted at thirty cash per dou; silk and satin clothing was reckoned at one string per bolt.

sentences.zh: 布每匹三百五十文，綿每兩四十文。

translations.literal: Cloth was three hundred fifty cash per bolt; cotton was forty cash per ounce.
translations.idiomatic: Plain cloth was valued at three hundred fifty cash per bolt and cotton at forty cash per ounce.

sentences.zh: 公用錢

translations.literal: Public-use funds.
translations.idiomatic: Public-Use Funds

sentences.zh: 自節度使兼使相，有給二萬貫者。

translations.literal: From military commissioners who also held envoy-chancellor status, some were granted twenty thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioners who also held concurrent envoy-chancellor titles could receive as much as twenty thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 其次萬貫至七千貫，凡四等。

translations.literal: Next were ten thousand strings down to seven thousand strings, four grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: The next tier ranged from ten thousand strings down to seven thousand, in four grades.

sentences.zh: 節度使，萬貫至三千貫，凡四等。

translations.literal: Military commissioners: ten thousand strings down to three thousand strings, four grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Military commissioners received from ten thousand strings down to three thousand, in four grades.

sentences.zh: 節度觀察留後，五千貫至二千貫，凡四等。

translations.literal: Military commissioner and observation commissioner acting deputies: five thousand strings down to two thousand strings, four grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Acting deputies for military and observation commissioners received from five thousand strings down to two thousand, in four grades.

sentences.zh: 觀察使，三千貫至二千五百貫，凡二等。

translations.literal: Observation commissioners: three thousand strings down to two thousand five hundred strings, two grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioners received from three thousand strings down to two thousand five hundred, in two grades.

sentences.zh: 防禦使，三千貫至千五百貫，凡四等。

translations.literal: Defense commissioners: three thousand strings down to one thousand five hundred strings, four grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Defense commissioners received from three thousand strings down to one thousand five hundred, in four grades.

sentences.zh: 團練使，二千貫至千貫，凡三等。

translations.literal: Training commissioners: two thousand strings down to one thousand strings, three grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Training commissioners received from two thousand strings down to one thousand, in three grades.

sentences.zh: 刺史，千五百貫至五百貫，凡三等。

translations.literal: Regional inspectors: one thousand five hundred strings down to five hundred strings, three grades in all.
translations.idiomatic: Regional inspectors received from one thousand five hundred strings down to five hundred, in three grades.

sentences.zh: 亦有不給者。

translations.literal: There were also some who received nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Some offices received no allotment at all.

sentences.zh: （觀察使以下在禁軍校者，皆不給。）

translations.literal: (Observation commissioners and below who served as academy officers in the Palace Guard all received nothing.)
translations.idiomatic: (Observation commissioners and below who held Palace Guard academy posts received nothing.)

sentences.zh: 京守在邊要或加錢給者，罷者如故，皆隨月給受，如祿奉焉。

translations.literal: Capital prefects on critical frontiers who received supplemental cash grants, when removed, remained as before; all received monthly disbursements like salary allotments.
translations.idiomatic: Capital-area prefects on vital frontiers who received supplemental payments continued at the same rate after removal; all were paid monthly like regular salaries.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，令河北、河東、陝西諸州，皆逐季給。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, an order required all prefectures in Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi to pay by season.]
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 5, all prefectures in Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi were ordered to pay quarterly.]

sentences.zh: 京師月給者：玉清昭應宮使，百千。

translations.literal: Those receiving monthly grants in the capital: Commissioner of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace, one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Monthly grants in the capital: the Commissioner of the Yuqing Zhaoying Palace received one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 景靈宮使，崇文院，七十千。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Jingling Palace, Chongwen Academy, seventy thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Jingling Palace and the Chongwen Academy each received seventy thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 會靈觀使，六十千。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Huiling Observatory, sixty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Commissioner of the Huiling Observatory received sixty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 祥源觀都大管勾，五十千。

translations.literal: Chief superintendent of the Xiangyuan Observatory, fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The chief superintendent of the Xiangyuan Observatory received fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 御史臺，三百千。

translations.literal: Censorate, three hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate received three hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 大理寺，二百五十三千。

translations.literal: Court of Judicial Review, two hundred fifty-three thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review received two hundred fifty-three thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 刑部，九十六千。

translations.literal: Ministry of Justice, ninety-six thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice received ninety-six thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 舍人院，二十千。

translations.literal: Drafting Academy, twenty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Drafting Academy received twenty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 太常寺，二十五千，秘閣，二十千。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices, twenty-five thousand cash; Imperial Archives, twenty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices received twenty-five thousand cash and the Imperial Archives twenty thousand.

sentences.zh: 宗正寺，十五千。

translations.literal: Imperial Clan Court, fifteen thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Clan Court received fifteen thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 太常禮院，起居院，十千。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Institute, Daily Records Institute, ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices Rites Institute and the Daily Records Institute each received ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 門下省，登聞檢院、鼓院，官誥院，三班院，各五十千。

translations.literal: Gate Department, Petition Review Institute, Drum Institute, Patent Office, Three-Rank Institute, each fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Department, the Petition Review and Drum institutes, the Patent Office, and the Three-Rank Institute each received fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 歲給者：尚書都省，銀台司，審刑院，提舉諸司庫務司，每給三十千，用盡續給，不限年月；

translations.literal: Those receiving annual grants: the Secretariat Directorate, Silver Terrace Office, Judicial Review Institute, and Intendant of the Various Bureau Storehouses Office each received thirty thousand cash, with renewal when exhausted, without limit by year or month;
translations.idiomatic: Annual grants went to the Secretariat Directorate, Silver Terrace Office, Judicial Review Institute, and the intendant of bureau storehouses; each received thirty thousand cash, replenished when spent, with no fixed term;

sentences.zh: 餘文武常參官內職知州者，歲給王千至百千，凡十三等，皆長吏與通判署籍連署以給用；

translations.literal: The remaining civil and military officials in regular audience who held inner-service posts as prefects received annual grants from five thousand cash to one hundred thousand cash, thirteen grades in all; the chief administrator and vice prefect registered and countersigned to disburse them;
translations.idiomatic: Other civil and military officials in regular audience who served as inner-court appointees as prefects received annual grants from five thousand to one hundred thousand cash in thirteen grades, disbursed on registers countersigned by the chief administrator and vice prefect;

sentences.zh: 少卿監以上，有增十千至百千者。

translations.literal: For vice directors of courts and commissions and above, some had increases from ten thousand cash to one hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors of courts and commissions and above could receive supplements from ten thousand up to one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年九月，詔諸州、軍、監、縣無公使處，遇誕降節給茶宴錢，節度州百千，防、團、刺史州五十千，監、三泉縣三十千，嶺南州、軍以幕府州縣官權知州十千。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Chunhua, an edict ordered that where prefectures, armies, directorates, and counties lacked public-use envoys, on imperial birthday and amnesty festivals tea-banquet funds were granted: military commissioner prefectures one hundred thousand cash; defense, training, and inspector prefectures fifty thousand cash; directorates and Sanquan County thirty thousand cash; Lingnan prefectures and armies gave ten thousand cash to staff prefecture and county officials acting as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Chunhua 1, where prefectures, armies, directorates, and counties had no public-use funds, birthday and amnesty festivals brought tea-banquet grants: military commissioner prefectures one hundred thousand cash, defense/training/inspector prefectures fifty thousand, directorates and Sanquan County thirty thousand, and in Lingnan ten thousand cash to staff officials acting as prefect.

sentences.zh: 文武君臣奉使於外，藩郡入朝，皆往來備饔餼，又有賓幕、軍將、隨身、牙官，馬驢、橐駝之差：節、察俱有賓幕以下；

translations.literal: Civil and military ministers and subjects on missions abroad and feudatory prefectures coming to court all had traveling provisions supplied; there were also differences in guest secretaries, military aides, personal attendants, yamen officers, horses, donkeys, and camels: military commissioners and observation commissioners all had guest secretaries and below;
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials on foreign missions and feudatory prefects attending court were supplied traveling provisions, with graded entourages of guest secretaries, military aides, personal attendants, yamen officers, horses, donkeys, and camels: military and observation commissioners received guest secretaries and the ranks below;

sentences.zh: 中書、樞密、三司使有隨身而無牙官、軍將隨；

translations.literal: The Central Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Commissioners of the Three Departments had personal attendants but no yamen officers or military aides accompanying;
translations.idiomatic: Central Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Three Departments commissioners had personal attendants but no yamen officers or military aides;

sentences.zh: 諸司使以上有軍將、橐駝。

translations.literal: Commissioners of the various bureaus and above had military aides and camels.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioners and above had military aides and camels.

sentences.zh: 餘皆有牙官、馬驢）〉

translations.literal: the rest all had yamen officers, horses, and donkeys.)
translations.idiomatic: All others had yamen officers, horses, and donkeys.)

sentences.zh: ，惟節、察有賓幕。

translations.literal: , only military commissioners and observation commissioners had guest secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Only military and observation commissioners had guest secretaries.

sentences.zh: 諸州及四夷貢奉使，諸司職掌祗事者，亦有給焉。

translations.literal: Prefectures and the four barbarians' tribute envoys, and officials of the various bureaus charged with attending duties, also had grants.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural offices, envoys from the four frontier peoples, and bureau officials on attending duty also received grants.

sentences.zh: 四夷有譯語、通事、書狀、換醫、十券頭、首領、部署、子弟之名，貢奉使有廳頭、子將、推船、防授之名，職掌有傔。

translations.literal: The four barbarians had titles such as interpreter, liaison, clerk, exchange physician, ten-coupon head, chief, deployment officer, and junior attendant; tribute envoys had hall head, sub-captain, boat-pusher, and patrol officer; attending officials had retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier missions used ranks such as interpreter, liaison, clerk, exchange physician, ten-coupon head, chief, deployment officer, and junior attendant; tribute envoys used hall head, sub-captain, boat-pusher, and patrol officer; attending officials had retainers.

sentences.zh: 京朝官、三班外任無添給者，止續給之。

translations.literal: Metropolitan officials and Three-Rank appointees on outer assignment without supplemental grants received only continued grants.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan officials and Three-Rank appointees serving outside the capital without supplemental grants received only continuing allotments.

sentences.zh: 京府按事畿內，幕職、州縣出境比較錢穀，覆按刑獄，並給券。

translations.literal: The capital prefecture investigating cases within the metropolitan circuit, secretariat staff, and prefecture and county officials leaving the border to compare revenue grain, or to review criminal cases, all received vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prefectural investigators in the metropolitan circuit, secretariat staff, and prefectural or county officials who left their jurisdiction to audit revenue grain or review criminal cases all received travel vouchers.

sentences.zh: 其赴任川峽者，給驛券，赴福建、廣南者，所過給倉券，入本路給驛券，皆至任則止。

translations.literal: Those taking up posts in the Chuan and Xia regions received relay vouchers; those going to Fujian and Guangnan received warehouse vouchers along the route and relay vouchers upon entering their circuit; all ceased upon arrival.
translations.idiomatic: Appointees to the Sichuan gorges received relay vouchers; those bound for Fujian and Guangnan received warehouse vouchers en route and relay vouchers after entering their circuit; all vouchers expired on reaching post.

sentences.zh: 車駕巡幸，群臣扈從者，中書、樞密、三司使給館券，餘官給倉券。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured, among the ministers following in attendance, the Central Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Three Departments commissioners received lodge vouchers; other officials received warehouse vouchers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, accompanying ministers from the Central Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, and Three Departments received lodge vouchers; all other officials received warehouse vouchers.

sentences.zh: 周自卿以下有圭田不稅，晉有芻田，後魏宰人之官有公田，北齊一品以下公田有差，唐制內外官各給職田，五代以來遂廢。

translations.literal: Under Zhou, from minister downward there were gui fields untaxed; Jin had fodder fields; Northern Wei had public fields for steward officials; Northern Qi had graded public fields below first rank; Tang's system granted duty fields to inner and outer officials alike; since the Five Dynasties it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou, ministers and below held tax-exempt gui fields; Jin had fodder fields; Northern Wei gave steward officials public fields; Northern Qi graded public fields below first rank; Tang allotted duty fields to civil officials inside and outside the capital; since the Five Dynasties the practice had lapsed.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，令館閣檢校故事。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era, an order directed the palace libraries to collate precedents.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping period, the palace libraries were ordered to collate historical precedents.

sentences.zh: 申定其制，以官莊及遠年逃亡田充。

translations.literal: They reported and fixed the system, filling it with official estates and fields long abandoned through flight.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted a fixed system, supplying fields from official estates and long-abandoned fugitive holdings.

sentences.zh: 悉免租稅，佃戶以浮客充，所得課租均分，如鄉原例。

translations.literal: All were exempted from rent and tax; tenants were filled with floating clients; collected field rents were divided equally, as in village custom.
translations.idiomatic: All such land was exempted from rent and tax; tenants were drawn from migrant laborers; collected rents were shared equally according to local village practice.

sentences.zh: 州縣長吏給十之五。

translations.literal: Prefecture and county chief administrators received five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county chief administrators received half the yield.

sentences.zh: 自餘差給。

translations.literal: The remainder was allotted by grade.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder was allotted by rank.

sentences.zh: 其兩京、大藩府四十頃，次藩鎮三十五頃，防禦、團練州三十頃，中、上刺史州二十頃，下州及軍、監十五頃，邊遠小州、上縣十頃，中縣八頃，下縣七頃，轉運使、副十頃，兵馬都監押、砦主、厘務官、錄事參軍、判司等，比通判、幕職之數而均給之。

translations.literal: The two capitals and great feudatory prefectures received forty qing; secondary feudatory prefectures thirty-five qing; defense and training prefectures thirty qing; middle and upper inspector prefectures twenty qing; lower prefectures and armies and directorates fifteen qing; remote small prefectures and upper counties ten qing; middle counties eight qing; lower counties seven qing; transport commissioners and deputies ten qing; commanders of armies and horses, stockade chiefs, administrative officers, recording secretaries, judicial clerks, and the like were compared to vice prefects and secretariat staff in number and allotted evenly.
translations.idiomatic: The two capitals and major prefectures received forty qing; secondary prefectures thirty-five; defense and training prefectures thirty; middle and upper inspector prefectures twenty; lower prefectures, armies, and directorates fifteen; remote small prefectures and upper counties ten; middle counties eight; lower counties seven; transport commissioners and deputies ten; army commanders, stockade chiefs, administrative officers, recording secretaries, and judicial clerks were matched to vice prefects and secretariat staff and allotted proportionally.

sentences.zh: 景德二年七月，詔諸州職田如有災傷，準例蠲課。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Jingde, an edict ordered that where prefectural duty fields suffered disaster or injury, rents were remitted according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Jingde 2, prefectural duty fields damaged by disaster were to have rents remitted according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，殿中侍御史王奇上言，請天下納職田以助振貨。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Qi memorialized, requesting that the empire surrender duty fields to aid relief grain.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 9, Palace Attendant Censor Wang Qi proposed surrendering duty fields empire-wide to fund relief grain.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「奇未曉給納之理。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Qi does not understand the principle of granting and surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Qi does not understand how grants and returns are supposed to work.

sentences.zh: 然朕每覽法寺奏款，外官占田多窬往製，不能自備牛種，水旱之際又不蠲省，致民無告。

translations.literal: Yet whenever I review the Judicial Review Court's submitted cases, outer officials' occupied fields often exceed former regulations; they cannot supply their own oxen and seed; in flood and drought they do not reduce exactions, causing the people to have nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever I read the Judicial Review Court's reports, outer officials' holdings often exceed the old quotas; they cannot supply their own oxen and seed, and in flood or drought they fail to reduce collections, leaving the people with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷奇奏，因下詔戒飭之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Qi's memorial was set aside, and an edict of admonition was issued.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi's proposal was rejected, and an edict of admonition was issued.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，上患職田有無不均，吏或多取以病民；

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era, the emperor worried that duty fields were uneven in presence and absence, and clerks often took too much and harmed the people;
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng period, the emperor worried that duty-field allotments were uneven and that clerks often over-collected and harmed the people;

sentences.zh: 詔罷天下職田，悉以歲入租課送官，具數上三司，計直而均給之。

translations.literal: an edict abolished duty fields empire-wide; all annual field rents were sent to government, the totals reported to the Three Departments, their value calculated and allotted evenly.
translations.idiomatic: an edict abolished duty fields empire-wide, required annual rents to be sent to government, reported to the Three Departments, valued in cash, and distributed evenly.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方議措置未下，仁宗閱具獄，見吏以賄敗者多，惻然傷之；

translations.literal: The court was still deliberating measures that had not been issued when Emperor Renzong reviewed the docket of cases and saw many clerks ruined by bribery; he was moved with compassion;
translations.idiomatic: While the court was still debating implementation, Emperor Renzong reviewed case files, saw how many officials had been ruined by bribery, and was deeply moved;

sentences.zh: 詔復給職田，毋多占佃戶，及無田而配出所租，違者以枉法論。

translations.literal: an edict restored duty fields, forbidding excessive occupation of tenants and assigning rents where there was no field; violators were prosecuted as bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered duty fields restored, forbade seizing excess tenants or assigning rents without land, and made violations a capital corruption offense.

sentences.zh: 又十餘年，至慶曆中，詔限職田，有司始申定其數。

translations.literal: After more than ten years, by the Qingli era, an edict limited duty fields and the responsible offices first reported and fixed the amounts.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later, in the Qingli period, an edict capped duty fields and the responsible offices first reported fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡大藩長吏二十頃，通判八頃，判官五頃，幕職官四頃。

translations.literal: In general, great feudatory chief administrators twenty qing, vice prefects eight qing, judicial officials five qing, secretariat staff four qing.
translations.idiomatic: For major prefectures: chief administrators twenty qing, vice prefects eight, judicial officials five, secretariat staff four.

sentences.zh: 凡節鎮長吏十五頃，通判七頃，判官四頃，幕職官三頃五十畝。

translations.literal: In general, military commissioner prefecture chief administrators fifteen qing, vice prefects seven qing, judicial officials four qing, secretariat staff three qing fifty mu.
translations.idiomatic: For military commissioner prefectures: chief administrators fifteen qing, vice prefects seven, judicial officials four, secretariat staff three qing fifty mu.

sentences.zh: 凡防、團以下州軍長吏十頃，通判六頃，判官三頃五十畝，幕職官三頃。

translations.literal: In general, defense and training prefectures and armies below them: chief administrators ten qing, vice prefects six qing, judicial officials three qing fifty mu, secretariat staff three qing.
translations.idiomatic: For defense and training prefectures and lower armies: chief administrators ten qing, vice prefects six, judicial officials three qing fifty mu, secretariat staff three qing.

sentences.zh: 其餘軍、監長吏七頃，判官、幕官，並同防、團以下州軍。

translations.literal: The remaining armies and directorates: chief administrators seven qing; judicial officials and secretariat staff the same as defense and training prefectures and armies below.
translations.idiomatic: Other armies and directorates: chief administrators seven qing; judicial and secretariat staff matched defense and training prefectures below.

sentences.zh: 凡縣令，萬戶以上六頃，五千戶以上五頃，不滿五千戶並四頃。

translations.literal: In general, county magistrates: ten thousand households and above six qing; five thousand households and above five qing; below five thousand households all four qing.
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates: six qing for counties of ten thousand households or more, five for five thousand or more, four for fewer than five thousand.

sentences.zh: 凡簿、尉，萬戶以上三頃，五千戶以上二頃五十畝，不滿五千戶二頃。

translations.literal: In general, registrars and precinct captains: ten thousand households and above three qing; five thousand households and above two qing fifty mu; below five thousand households two qing.
translations.idiomatic: Registrars and precinct captains: three qing for ten thousand households or more, two qing fifty mu for five thousand or more, two qing below five thousand.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍比本判官。

translations.literal: Recording secretaries were compared to their prefecture's judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Recording secretaries matched their prefecture's judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 曹官比倚郭簿、尉。

translations.literal: Department clerks were compared to suburban registrars and precinct captains.
translations.idiomatic: Department clerks matched suburban registrars and precinct captains.

sentences.zh: 發運製置、轉運使副，武臣總管，比節鎮長吏。

translations.literal: Dispatch and transport establishment commissioners, transport deputy commissioners, and military circuit commanders were compared to military commissioner prefecture chief administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch establishment commissioners, transport deputies, and military circuit commanders matched military commissioner prefecture administrators.

sentences.zh: 發運製置判官，比大藩府通判。

translations.literal: Dispatch establishment judicial officials were compared to great feudatory vice prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch establishment judicial officials matched major prefectural vice prefects.

sentences.zh: 安撫都監，路分都監，比節鎮通判。

translations.literal: Pacification chief supervisors and circuit chief supervisors were compared to military commissioner vice prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification and circuit chief supervisors matched military commissioner vice prefects.

sentences.zh: 大藩府都監，比本府判官。

translations.literal: Great feudatory chief supervisors were compared to their prefecture's judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Major prefectural chief supervisors matched their prefecture's judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 黃汴河、許汝石塘河都大催綱，比節鎮判官。

translations.literal: Chief grain-transport superintendents of the Yellow Bian River and Xu-Ru Stone Pond River were compared to military commissioner judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chief transport superintendents on the Yellow Bian and Xu-Ru Stone Pond rivers matched military commissioner judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 節鎮以下至軍監，諸路走馬承受並砦主，都同巡檢，提舉捉賊，提點馬監，都大巡河，不得過節鎮判官。

translations.literal: From military commissioner prefectures down to armies and directorates, circuit mobile receivers and stockade chiefs, unified assistant inspectors, theft-intendant posts, horse-directorate intendants, and chief river patrol officers could not exceed military commissioner judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: From military commissioner prefectures down through armies and directorates, circuit mobile receivers, stockade chiefs, unified assistant inspectors, theft intendants, horse intendants, and chief river patrol officers could not exceed military commissioner judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 在州監當及催綱、撥發，巡捉私茶鹽賊盜，駐泊捉賊，不得過簿、尉。

translations.literal: In-prefecture superintendents, transport urging and dispatch, patrols against private tea and salt smuggling, and moored theft-capture posts could not exceed registrars and precinct captains.
translations.idiomatic: In-prefecture superintendents, transport urging and dispatch, private tea-and-salt patrols, and moored theft-capture posts could not exceed registrars and precinct captains.

sentences.zh: 自此人有定制，士有定限，吏以職田抵罪者，視昔為庶幾焉。

translations.literal: From this, people had fixed regulations, scholars had fixed limits, and officials prosecuted for duty-field offenses were, compared with the past, nearly improved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter quotas were fixed for officials and scholars alike, and prosecutions for duty-field abuses came far closer to the intended standard than before.

sentences.zh: 至熙寧間，復詔詳定：

translations.literal: By the Xining era, an edict again ordered detailed determination:
translations.idiomatic: In the Xining period, another edict ordered a detailed revision:

sentences.zh: 凡知大藩府三京、京兆、成都、太原、荊南、江寧府，延、秦、揚、杭、潭、廣州。

translations.literal: In general, those who governed great feudatory prefectures: the three capitals, Jingzhao, Chengdu, Taiyuan, Jingnan, Jiangning prefectures, Yan'an, Qin, Yang, Hang, Tan, and Guang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Great prefectures governed directly included the three capitals plus Jingzhao, Chengdu, Taiyuan, Jingnan, and Jiangning, and Yan'an, Qin, Yang, Hang, Tan, and Guang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 二十頃，節鎮十五頃，餘州及軍淮陽、無為、臨江、廣德、興國、南康、南安、建昌、邵武、興化。

translations.literal: twenty qing; military commissioner prefectures fifteen qing; remaining prefectures and armies Huaiyang, Wuwei, Linjiang, Guangde, Xingguo, Nankang, Nan'an, Jianchang, Shaowu, Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty qing; military commissioner prefectures fifteen; other prefectures and the armies Huaiyang, Wuwei, Linjiang, Guangde, Xingguo, Nankang, Nan'an, Jianchang, Shaowu, and Xinghua

sentences.zh: 並十頃，餘小軍、監七頃。

translations.literal: all ten qing; remaining small armies and directorates seven qing.
translations.idiomatic: each received ten qing; other small armies and directorates seven qing.

sentences.zh: 通判、藩府八頃，節鎮七頃，餘州六頃。

translations.literal: Vice prefects: feudatory prefectures eight qing, military commissioner prefectures seven qing, remaining prefectures six qing.
translations.idiomatic: Vice prefects: eight qing in feudatory prefectures, seven in military commissioner prefectures, six in other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 留守、節度、觀察判官，藩府五頃，節鎮四頃。

translations.literal: Judicial officials of garrison commissioners, military commissioners, and observation commissioners: feudatory prefectures five qing, military commissioner prefectures four qing.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison, military, and observation commissioners' judicial officials: five qing in feudatory prefectures, four in military commissioner prefectures.

sentences.zh: 掌書記以下幕職官三頃五十畝。

translations.literal: Secretariat staff from recorder downward: three qing fifty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat staff from the recorder down: three qing fifty mu.

sentences.zh: 防禦、團練軍事推官，軍、監判官三頃。

translations.literal: Defense and training military affairs investigating officials, army and directorate judicial officials: three qing.
translations.idiomatic: Defense and training investigating officials and army or directorate judicial officials: three qing.

sentences.zh: 令、丞、簿、尉。

translations.literal: Magistrates, assistants, registrars, precinct captains.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates, assistants, registrars, and precinct captains.

sentences.zh: 萬戶以上，縣令六頃，丞四頃；

translations.literal: Ten thousand households and above: county magistrate six qing, assistant four qing;
translations.idiomatic: For counties of ten thousand households or more: magistrates six qing, assistants four;

sentences.zh: 不滿萬戶，令五頃，丞三頃；

translations.literal: Below ten thousand households: magistrate five qing, assistant three qing;
translations.idiomatic: Below ten thousand households: magistrates five qing, assistants three;

sentences.zh: 不滿五千戶，令四頃，丞二頃五十畝。

translations.literal: Below five thousand households: magistrate four qing, assistant two qing fifty mu.
translations.idiomatic: Below five thousand households: magistrates four qing, assistants two qing fifty mu.

sentences.zh: 簿、尉減令之半。

translations.literal: Registrars and precinct captains were reduced by half from the magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Registrars and precinct captains received half the magistrate's allotment.

sentences.zh: 藩府、節鎮錄參，視本州判官，餘視幕職官。

translations.literal: Feudatory and military commissioner recording secretaries were treated as their prefecture's judicial officials; the rest were treated as secretariat staff.
translations.idiomatic: Recording secretaries in feudatory and military commissioner prefectures matched their prefecture's judicial officials; others matched secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 藩府、節鎮曹官，視萬戶縣簿、尉，餘視不滿萬戶者。

translations.literal: Feudatory and military commissioner department clerks were treated as registrars and precinct captains of ten-thousand-household counties; the rest as below ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Department clerks in feudatory and military commissioner prefectures matched registrars and captains in ten-thousand-household counties; others matched counties below that threshold.

sentences.zh: 發運、轉運使、副，視節鎮知州。

translations.literal: Dispatch and transport commissioners and deputies were treated as military commissioner prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch and transport commissioners and deputies matched military commissioner prefects.

sentences.zh: 開封府界提點，視餘州。

translations.literal: Kaifeng prefectural circuit intendants were treated as remaining prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng circuit intendants matched other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 發運、轉運判官，常平倉司提舉官，視藩府通判。

translations.literal: Dispatch and transport judicial officials and Ever-Normal Granary intendants were treated as feudatory vice prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch and transport judicial officials and Ever-Normal Granary intendants matched feudatory vice prefects.

sentences.zh: 同提舉，視萬戶縣令。

translations.literal: Associate intendants were treated as magistrates of ten-thousand-household counties.
translations.idiomatic: Associate intendants matched magistrates of ten-thousand-household counties.

sentences.zh: 發運司幹當公事，視節鎮通判。

translations.literal: Dispatch Transport Bureau officers who handled public affairs were treated as military commissioner vice prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Officers handling routine affairs in the Dispatch Transport Bureau matched military commissioner vice prefects in their office-land allotments.

sentences.zh: 轉運司管幹文字，提刑司檢法官，提舉常平倉司幹當公事，視不滿萬戶縣令。

translations.literal: Transport Circuit supervising document clerks, penal intendant judicial examiners, and Ever-Normal Granary Bureau officers handling public affairs were treated as magistrates of counties below ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Transport circuit document supervisors, penal intendant judicial examiners, and Ever-Normal Granary routine officers were allotted like magistrates of counties with fewer than ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 蔡河、許汝石塘河都大催綱，管幹機宜文字，府界提點司幹當公事，視節鎮判官。

translations.literal: Chief grain-escort supervisors of the Cai River, Xu-Ru Stone Pond River, policy text managers, and prefectural-circuit intendant bureau officers handling public affairs were treated as military commissioner judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Chief escort supervisors on the Cai and Xu-Ru canals, policy text managers, and Kaifeng circuit intendant routine officers matched military commissioner judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 總管，視節鎮知州。

translations.literal: Overall supervisors were treated as military commissioner prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Overall supervisors received the same allotment as military commissioner prefects.

sentences.zh: 路分鈐轄，視餘州知州。

translations.literal: Circuit security commissioners were treated as prefects of the remaining prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit security commissioners matched prefects in ordinary prefectures.

sentences.zh: 安撫、路分都監，州鈐轄，視節鎮通判。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioners, circuit military superintendents, and prefectural security commissioners were treated as military commissioner vice prefects.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification commissioners, circuit military superintendents, and prefectural security commissioners were allotted like military commissioner vice prefects.

sentences.zh: 藩府都監，視本州判官。

translations.literal: Feudatory prefecture military superintendents were treated as their own prefecture's judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Military superintendents in feudatory prefectures matched their prefecture's judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 諸路正將，視路分都監；

translations.literal: Circuit chief commanders were treated as circuit military superintendents;
translations.idiomatic: Chief commanders on the circuits matched circuit military superintendents;

sentences.zh: 副將，視藩府都監。

translations.literal: deputy commanders were treated as feudatory military superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: deputy commanders matched feudatory military superintendents.

sentences.zh: 走馬承受，諸州都監，都同巡，都大巡河，並視節鎮判官。

translations.literal: Palace relay commissioners, prefectural military superintendents, chief joint patrol officers, and chief river patrol officers were all treated as military commissioner judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Palace relay commissioners, prefectural military superintendents, chief joint patrol officers, and chief river patrol officers alike matched military commissioner judicial officials.

sentences.zh: 巡檢，堡砦都監，砦主，在州監當及催綱、撥發，巡捉私茶鹽賊盜，駐泊捉賊，並視幕職官。

translations.literal: Inspectors, fort and stockade military superintendents, stockade chiefs, in-prefecture supervisors and grain-escort and dispatch officers, patrol officers for illicit tea, salt, and bandits, and moored seizure officers were all treated as secretariat staff.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors, fort and stockade superintendents, stockade chiefs, prefectural supervisors of escort and dispatch duties, private tea-and-salt patrols, and moored bandit-capture posts were all allotted like secretariat staff.

sentences.zh: 巡轄馬遞鋪，監堰並縣、鎮、砦監當，並視本縣簿、尉。

translations.literal: Patrol officers over courier relay stations, dike supervisors, and county, market, and stockade supervisors were all treated as their county's registrars and precinct captains.
translations.idiomatic: Relay-station patrol officers, dike supervisors, and supervisors in counties, markets, and stockades matched their county registrars and precinct captains.

sentences.zh: 諸路州學教授，京朝視本州判官，選人視本州曹官。

translations.literal: Prefectural school instructors on the circuits: metropolitan officials were treated as their prefecture's judicial officials; selected officials were treated as their prefecture's department clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural instructors on the circuits: metropolitan appointees matched their prefecture's judicial officials, while selected officials matched its department clerks.

sentences.zh: 又詔：「成都府路提點刑獄司，以本路職田令逐州軍歲以子利稻麥等拘收變錢，從本司以一路所收錢數，又紐而為斛斗價直，然後等第均給。

translations.literal: Another edict stated: "The Chengdu Circuit Office for Intending Penal Affairs shall, using this circuit's office lands, order each prefecture and commandery yearly to seize and convert subsidiary yields of rice, wheat, and the like into cash; the office shall then, from the cash totals collected on the whole circuit, convert them again into bushel-and-picul values, and only then distribute by graded ranks."

translations.idiomatic: To spare the people, vice prefects and magistrates were charged to verify holdings, remove land that could not be farmed, and cut excessive fixed quotas.

sentences.zh: 凡職租不許輒令保正催納，或抑令折納見錢，或無田平白監租，或以虛數勒民代納，或額外過數多取，皆申嚴禁止之令。

translations.literal: In general, office rent was not permitted to be hastily made ward chiefs collect, or coerced into commutation to ready cash, or supervised rent on no fields in plain white, or compelled by false numbers for the people to pay in proxy, or taken beyond the quota in excessive numbers — all were to announce strict prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Office rent could not be casually collected by ward chiefs, commuted under coercion to cash, levied where no land existed, extorted through fictitious figures, or taken above quota — strict prohibitions were proclaimed for all such abuses.

sentences.zh: 察以監司，坐以贓罪，所以防其不廉之害。

translations.literal: Inspection was by supervisory commissioners; conviction was under booty offenses — this was to guard against the harm of lack of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisory commissioners were to investigate, and offenders were to be punished for illicit gain — measures against corruption.

sentences.zh: 罷廢未幾而復舊，拘借未久而給還，移充糴本，轉收馬料，旋復免行，皆所以示優恩，厲清操也。

translations.literal: Abolished not long before and then restored to the old, seized on loan not long before and then returned, shifted to fill grain-purchase capital, turned to collect horse fodder, then soon again exempted from execution — all were to display gracious favor and encourage pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Office lands were briefly abolished and then restored, briefly seized and soon returned, diverted to grain purchases or horse fodder and then quickly exempted again — each reversal meant to show favor while urging clean conduct.

translations.idiomatic: The prescribed acreage was set by fixed rules: prefects of feudatory prefectures,
